subject: general
question: To which group of temples does Kandariya Mahadev Temple belong?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khajuraho Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Khajuraho Temple**

 
 
• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments is a group of Hindu temples and Jain temples in the Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh.
 
• They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The temples are famous for their nagara-style architecture.
 
• The city of the temples is famous for the Khajuraho Temples built with folded stones all over the world.
 
• This city was the first capital of the Chandel empire.
 
• The Chandel Dynasty and the founder of Khajuraho were Chandravarman.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

__
 
• **Konark Sun Temple:__

 __
 
• It is situated at Konark in Odisha.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It is dedicated to the sun god, Surya, the first rays of the sun fall on the entrance of the temple.
 
• It was built in the 13th century and was built by King Narasimhadeva I.
 
• This temple also is known as the "Black Pagoda".
 
 
 
• ​Ellora Cave Temple**
 
 
• The Kailash temple at Ellora is an example of the Rock-cut temple__.
 
• It is one of the largest rock-cut ancient Hindu temples in India, made up of a large single rock in Maharashtra.
 
• The Kailash Temple is the sixteenth cave, and it is one of the 32 cave temples and monasteries forming the magnanimous Ellora Caves.
 
• As per the historical records, it was built by the 8th century Rashtrakuta King Krishna I (756-773 AD).
 
 
 
• **Mahabalipuram Temple**
 
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram is an example of the Dravidian school of temple architecture: 
 
• The Shore Temple is a prime example of the Dravidian style, which was popular during the Pallava Dynasty.
 
• It's considered one of the earliest examples of Dravidian architecture. 
 
• The Shore Temple is a symbol of religious harmony, as it has sacred spaces dedicated to both Shiva and Vishnu.
 
• It was also an important symbol of Pallava's political and economic strength. 
 
• The Shore Temple demonstrates the progression from rock-cut structures to free-standing structural temples. 
 
• The Shore Temple's architecture has inspired temples across South India constructed in the Dravidian style. 
 
 

1d
